title: Shipping Changes: Shadow, Canary and Rollback
summary: Changing a prompt, a model or a retriever can quietly break an LLM feature. This lesson shows how to introduce changes safely: why offline tests miss regressions, shadow traffic, canary sizing with the 1 − (1 − p)^n rule, guard metrics, rollback and a staged playbook.
objectives: Explain why LLM changes need production-style testing beyond an offline evaluation set
Design a shadow deployment and compare candidate and baseline outputs
Size a canary using the probability of seeing at least one failure and estimate detection time
Choose guard metrics and thresholds that trigger automatic rollback
Plan a staged rollout with gates, holds and a tested rollback path
prerequisites: You should be comfortable with the evaluation basics from [Comparing Systems You Can Trust](/learn/evaluation/comparing-systems), with error rates and SLOs from [Observability and Incident Analysis](/learn/production-systems/observability), and with independent-event probabilities.
